subject: Streaming queue priority causing intermittent customer timeouts
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, natalie@nimbleretail.com, eric.gomez@nimbleretail.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Streaming queue priority causing intermittent customer timeouts

Eric / Natalie — looping in Platform & PM because we're seeing repeated 504 timeouts from Nimble's integration while using streaming completions. They report that requests either stall for ~20s or return an immediate 504, typically after the first 2-3 tokens stream successfully. Attached trace and the steps Nimble used to reproduce.

What I can tell from the trace: repeated log lines like:
  STREAM: dropped priority=0x03 seq=...
  CLIENT-RESP: 504 gateway timeout

Context:
- SDK: redwood-js v1.8.2 (they're on the latest public SDK)
- Model: openlm/gptx-7b (hosted on rw-prod with runtime v2.3.7)
- Workload: low concurrency (1-3 concurrent sessions), variable seq lengths

Ask:
1) Can runtime confirm whether the queue-priority change shipped in v2.3.7 could cause reordering or head-of-line blocking for streaming responses when KV cache is warming?
2) If that's feasible, can we get a short-term mitigation (config flag / canary) we can apply to Nimble's tenant or advise the SDK team on a client-side header workaround?

I've attached nimble_timeout_trace.log and nimble_repro_steps.md. Eric — can you confirm a good window to test a workaround this afternoon?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

----
Attachment: nimble_timeout_trace.log (text, 84KB)
Attachment: nimble_repro_steps.md (text, 2KB)

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: natalie@nimbleretail.com, eric.gomez@nimbleretail.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming queue priority causing intermittent customer timeouts

Thanks for the detailed repro + logs, Jasmine.

Short answer: yes, this looks like it maps to a regression we introduced last week when we changed the queue prioritization heuristics (commit 1a2b3c). The heuristic was intended to favor low-latency traffic but under certain KV-cache-warm conditions it can reorder stream fragments which causes the client-side stream handler to see an out-of-order chunk and treat it as a fatal error (we log as dropped/invalid and return 504).

Actionable items I can take immediately:
- I can build a canary image (runtime v2.3.8-canary) that disables the new reordering heuristic (runtime.allow_stream_reordering=false) and push it to canary today.
- As a short-term SDK workaround: set the X-Stream-Priority header to "normal" for streaming calls (that avoids the low-latency path). I'll sync with SDK leads on a quick patch note.

Request from my side:
- Can you share the full pod/instance IDs from the trace (lines at top of the log contain them) and confirm the exact timestamps for the reproduced failure? That will let me match server logs with the trace.
- If Nimble can toggle the header in a test run, we can validate within 30–45 minutes of the canary being live.

I'll prepare the canary and post the image name + deployment steps here once ready.

- Dev

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming queue priority causing intermittent customer timeouts

Eric — quick update from Platform: they believe the new queue-priority heuristic in runtime v2.3.7 can cause out-of-order chunks when the KV cache is warming, which is what your trace looks like.

Temporary workaround we can try right away (no infra change required): set the header X-Stream-Priority: normal on your streaming requests (this is a client-side change in the SDK call). Dev will stand by to validate when you test.

If you can run the repro script again with that header and paste the timestamp here, we can correlate. If that reduces failures we'll coordinate a canary for your tenant.

If you prefer, we can schedule the canary deploy (runtime v2.3.8-canary) to your tenant tonight so you don't have to change the client. Which do you prefer?

—Jasmine

Team — Nimble is a mid-market account in an active pilot; we've got usage and a near-term deal (see deal NIMB-2026-Q1-5243). This is priority-high.

Marissa: please work with Product/Platform to prioritize a hotfix and a canary schedule. Business asks:
- Can we get canary for Nimble tonight (US PST) and a full rollout in the low-traffic window tomorrow morning UTC?
- If rollout causes an error spike, what is rollback latency? Need an RTO estimate.
- Sales may need to offer a one-off credit if this impacted evaluation metrics — I'll draft the ask once we know customer impact.

Dev: please keep the SDK workaround in parallel; we want both paths (client header + canary) so customer can test quickly.

Thanks — please CC me on customer-facing notes.

Sergio
Head of Sales Operations
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: natalie@nimbleretail.com, eric.gomez@nimbleretail.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Streaming queue priority causing intermittent customer timeouts

Update: we've built v2.3.8-canary with the reordering heuristic disabled (runtime.allow_stream_reordering=false). Plan below:

Canary plan:
- Deploy v2.3.8-canary to canary pool at 17:30 PT today (2026-03-22).
- Monitor 15m windows for increased error rates and tail latency.
- If stable, schedule tenant rollout for Nimble on 2026-03-23 02:00 UTC (low-traffic window).
- Rollback is automated and should complete within ~4 minutes to revert to v2.3.7 if error rate increases > 2x baseline.

Customer-specific options:
- If Nimble wants to test before canary, add header X-Stream-Priority: normal in the SDK and run stream_repro_script.sh. Dev will watch logs.
- Post-canary we will expose a tenant-level flag (control-plane) to set runtime.allow_stream_reordering=false for specific tenants for immediate relief while we validate.

I'll post the canary image name and rollout job id once the deploy starts. Thanks for moving quickly — this looks like a clean regression so patching is low-risk.

- Dev

Attachment: stream_repro_script.sh (bash script, 1.5KB)

We'll stand by for the canary deploy and run a second validation after Nimble is moved to the canary image. Appreciate the quick response.
